messages:
sam: Quick follow-up to the sparse pages ownership RFC — I pushed a proposal for a lighter ownership model that avoids global refcounts. TL;DR: per-pool ownership + async return path. Thoughts?

rachel: moving away from a global refcount sounds good perf-wise. main worry: correctness for cross-pool aliasing (page mapped in GPU and host pools at once). how do we ensure we don't free under an alias?

sam: good call. proposal uses a lightweight pinned bit + epoch token instead of refcount. aliasing check: when another pool maps the page it must grab the pin (CAS on pinned bit). if it fails, it retries via slowpath and asks owner to handback.

lee: can you paste the pseudocode for the fastpath? want to see race window.

sam: sure:

```
bool try_pin(page_t *p) {
  uint32_t old = atomic_load(&p->state);
  if (old & PINNED) return false;
  return atomic_compare_exchange_weak(&p->state, &old, old | PINNED);
}

// fast allocate path
if (try_pin(p)) {
  // we now own a transient pin, safe to map
} else {
  // fallback: request owner -> slowpath handback
}
```

mike: i worry about livelock if lots of threads racing CAS and bouncing to slowpath. did you simulate under bursty inference?

sam: we ran a small sim: 64 threads, 90% map/unmap, skewed hotset. CAS success ~= 98% at 64 threads. slowpath rate grew linearly after 256 threads. resolution: exponential backoff + batching of handbacks.

rachel: what about accounting for residency/eviction? pinned bit prevents evict, but we need to respect tenant quotas. how does eviction interact with pinned pages?

sam: eviction policy sees pinned bit and treats pages as protected for a short grace window (epoch). owner can mark for demote; pinned pages will be demoted once pin is released. we also ship a per-tenant pinned_budget to avoid tenants pinning everything.

lee: interface boundary question: should pin/unpin be exposed to runtime callers (router/worker) or be internal to allocator? exposing it makes reward caching simpler but leaks complexity.

mike: prefer internal. callers should ask for a MappingHandle that auto-unpins on drop. keeps callers simple.

rachel: agree. plus metrics: we need pinned_hold_time histogram, pin_fail_rate, slowpath_count. add to console dashboards.

sam: noted — telemetry will include pinned_hold_time_ms, pin_cas_retries, slowpath_handbacks. default debug sampling 1% across prod.

lee: rollout plan? major runtime change, need canary + compatibility with old hostpage shim.

sam: plan: (1) feature-flag the new ownership model, (2) rollout to internal dev cluster, (3) enable for 10% of traffic in staging with heavy-embed workload, (4) monitor pin_fail_rate and tail latencies, (5) canary to 1% prod, then 10/50/100 if stable.

mike: tests? unit tests for CAS races, integration test that stresses aliasing (gpu+host map), and a perf harness comparing tokens/sec and p99. can we run perf on a reserved node?

sam: yes, i put a perf job in CI (jenkins job id: infra/sparse-pin-harness) — command: `tools/bench/run --profile sparse_pin --concurrency 128 --duration 2m`. results get uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/sparse-pin/173820.

rachel: another thought: what about interaction with KV cache? if we auto-evict pages while cache still references them we might get noise. ensure cache holds a MappingHandle or at least a soft pin.

sam: yes KV cache will hold a soft pin (counts towards pinned_budget but lower priority). soft pins can be preempted by owner eviction path with grace backoff.

lee: any ABI changes? public vmem API must remain stable for Private deployments.

sam: no public ABI changes. the switch is internal to the allocator and gated by feature flag. only optional telemetry tags added.

mike: sounds doable. last ask: can we add a diagnostic mode that, when enabled, logs slowpath handbacks with stack traces (sampled) to help triage?

sam: yes — devbot will toggle diag mode with `/feature sparse_pin_diag on` for a window. slowpath sampling at 10% in diag.

devbot: Feature flag `sparse_pin` created. rollout group: dev-internal. diag toggle: `sparse_pin_diag`.

rachel: action items: sam to land prototype PR, lee to add unit-race-tests, mike to prepare perf harness and reserved node, i'll add telemetry dashboards. target: land by EOW for internal trial.

sam: putting up PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 — comments welcome.

lee: will review today. thanks for the write-up, sam.

mike: queued the perf job, will post results to thread when done. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks all.
